requirements.requirement: On node1, local password authentication locks an account upon the fifth failed attempt, while four failures remain below the threshold.
requirements.summary: Both local PAM stacks contain deny=5 with account enforcement. A correct password succeeded after four recorded failures, while five failures produced five tally records and caused the correct password to be denied. The behavior was successfully repeated after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The account lockout lasts five minutes before authentication becomes available again.
requirements.summary: Both PAM stacks were configured with unlock_time=300, and that setting persisted through reboot. However, the evidence never waits through the interval or demonstrates automatic authentication recovery after approximately 300 seconds; tallies were manually reset during cleanup.

overall_summary: The task is partially satisfied: node1 demonstrably locks a local account on the fifth failed password authentication and not after four, with configuration and enforcement surviving a reboot. The configured timeout is 300 seconds, but five-minute automatic expiry was not behaviorally demonstrated. The mandatory restart protocol is otherwise complete for the sole managed node: healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered sshd/system state, retained PAM configuration, and a successful post-restart functional retest.
limitations: No bounded test demonstrated continued denial during the five-minute interval followed by automatic successful authentication after expiry.
Lifecycle package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently observed; the command trace contains no package-changing action.
The rollback backup created under /root was not included in final cleanup or inventory evidence, so its final presence cannot be directly confirmed.

The after-prepare snapshot aliases before-prepare because preparation was disabled; its boot-identity cross-check is therefore represented by global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity and compared with global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The PAM changes and rollback backup had a clear implementation/safety role; disposable users, credentials, tallies, mailboxes, and temporary outputs supported bounded functional tests and were ultimately removed. The reboot was required by the provider protocol. Final observations show no failed services, no test artifacts in the bounded temporary-file inventory, and the same listening services with only reboot-related PID changes. The only uncertainty is that the rollback directory created under /root was not included in the final inventory; its removal is not shown, but it is not classified as an unrelated or abandoned mutation because it served a clear rollback purpose.
